chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub Abul Hasan al-Ju'fi narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to me, from his father and Wahb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Qa'im will rise in an odd number of years: nine, one, three, five. And he said: When the Banu Umayya disagree and their kingdom passes away, then the Banu Abbas will rule. They will remain in the prime of kingship and abundance of livelihood until they disagree among themselves. When they disagree, their kingdom passes away, and the people of the East and the people of the West will disagree, yes, and the people of the Qibla. People will face severe hardship from the fear that passes over them. They will remain in that state until a caller from the sky calls out. When he calls, it is 'The call, the call.' By Allah, as if I see him between the Corner and the Maqam, the people are giving him allegiance with a new matter, a new book, and a new authority from the sky. Indeed, no flag will be defeated for him until he dies.

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ وَالْمَقَامُ: The Corner and the Maqam (stations) of the Kaaba in Mecca.
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam in his occultation who will rise to fill the earth with justice.
key_terms.وَتْرٍ مِنَ السِّنِينَ: Odd number of years, referring to the years 1, 3, 5, or 9 after the start of a cycle.

ai.seo_question: What is the sequence of political powers and signs preceding the rise of the Qa'im according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) details a specific geopolitical sequence where the Umayyad decline precedes the Abbasid golden age, which eventually fractures into internal strife and global turmoil. This period of intense fear culminates in a celestial announcement heralding the Qa'im, who establishes a 'new command' and 'new book' from heaven, ensuring his sovereignty remains unchallenged until his death. This narration underscores the transition from earthly political instability to divine authority, a core theme in Shia eschatology regarding the Mahdi's reappearance.
